title: Bourbon, Shallot and Pepper Pan Gravy
description: A small splash of bourbon lifts a smooth beef gravy flavored with sweet caramelized shallot and a little black pepper.

ingredients.name: finely minced shallot
ingredients.note: Caramelize completely before blending into the gravy.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable seasoning blend.

ingredients.name: bourbon
ingredients.note: Measure into a cup before approaching the stove.

steps.title: Caramelize the shallot
steps.text: Warm {shallot} in {butter} in the HexClad over medium-low heat for 12–18 minutes, stirring often. Add a little {broth} whenever the pan catches, until the shallot is uniformly soft and deep gold.

steps.title: Deglaze off the burner
steps.text: Move the skillet off the burner, away from the flame. Add the premeasured {bourbon} and the remaining {broth}, scraping the bottom with a silicone spoon.

steps.title: Infuse the pepper
steps.text: Return the pan to medium heat. Add {pepper} and simmer 4 minutes. Press the liquid and soft shallot through the sieve into a heatproof bowl, then return the smooth base to the pan.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Serve the gravy
steps.text: Divide the gravy between two portions of thinly sliced cooked beef, spooning it between the slices as well as over them.

notes: Make ahead: The caramelized shallot and broth base can be made a day ahead. Chill prepared gravy in a shallow covered container for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in individual portions for up to 2 months and whisk as it reheats. Fridge reheat: Warm in the HexClad over medium-low, stirring with a splash of water or broth if needed. Bring the whole sauce briefly to a rolling boil, then serve. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Whisk smooth and follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses bourbon and pepper. For gentler or alcohol-free Option B, replace the bourbon with extra broth and leave the pepper for the table. Use avocado oil in place of butter for dairy-free gravy.
